newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Midwest spot power lower again with weather.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Midwest spot power lower again with weather.

text.p: U.S. Midwest spot electricity was lower again Thursday with cool temperatures and clouds through much of the region, industry sources said.
"There seems to be a lot of energy around today, and prices are coming off again," one Mid-Continent Area Power Pool (MAPP) trader.

Some electricity producers were said to be backing off production at some coal units due to the lower prices, and in Minnesota two coal units with a total of 888 megawatts of capacity were off line for an unspecified time for repairs.

On-peak prices in the Mid-American Interpool Network (MAIN) for Friday delivery were said to be discussed in the $15.00-17.00 range from discussion at $21.00-25.00 per megawatt hour (MWh) on Wednesday, broker and marketers said.
In the MAPP region, on-peak power for Friday delivery was pegged in the $14.00-16.00 range from 14.50-17.00 on Wednesday, the sources said.
In the East Central Area Reliability Coordination Agreement (ECAR), peak power prices for Friday delivery were quoted at 16.50-18.00 from Wednesday talk at $17.00-19.00.
In the Southwest Power Pool (SPP), on-peak power for Friday delivery was assessed in the $13.00-15.00 range from $15.00-21.00 on Wednesday, the sources said.
